unit.title: Powers, Roots & Scientific Notation
unit.essential_question: How do powers, roots, and scientific notation help us represent scale, reveal patterns, and reason about quantities beyond ordinary size?
big_ideas: An exponent records repeated multiplication and must be interpreted with attention to the base and grouping.
Exponent properties follow from counting repeated factors and preserve equivalent value.
Roots undo powers and connect perfect squares and cubes with geometric measurement.
Irrational roots can be located and estimated using nearby perfect powers.
Scientific notation combines a coefficient with a power of ten to communicate scale efficiently and precisely.
unit.architecture: Integrated Grade 9 learning: instruction + reasoning + practice + application + tools + reflection + mastery
unit.tool_integration: Scientific calculator use is optional for verification, approximation, and scale exploration after students first record the mathematical model or reasoning.

lessons.title: Exponent Meaning, Powers & Grouping
objectives: Interpret exponential notation as repeated multiplication.
Identify the base, exponent, power, and value.
Evaluate powers with positive integer exponents.
Distinguish a negative base from a negative sign outside a power.

lessons.title: Exponent Patterns, Zero & Negative Exponents
objectives: Use patterns to explain the zero-exponent rule.
Interpret negative exponents as reciprocals.
Evaluate powers with integer exponents.
State restrictions involving a zero base.

lessons.title: Exponent Properties & Equivalent Expressions
objectives: Apply product and quotient properties for powers with the same base.
Apply the power-of-a-power property.
Use powers of products and quotients.
Check exponent-property results by expanding factors.

lessons.title: Square Roots, Cube Roots & Perfect Powers
objectives: Interpret square roots as inverse operations of squaring.
Evaluate principal square roots of perfect squares.
Evaluate cube roots of perfect cubes.
Connect roots with side length, area, edge length, and volume.

lessons.title: Estimating Irrational Roots & Comparing Values
objectives: Locate nonperfect square roots between consecutive integers.
Estimate square roots to a chosen decimal place.
Recognize common irrational roots.
Compare rational and irrational values on a number line.

lessons.title: Scientific Notation, Powers of Ten & Order of Magnitude
objectives: Write very large and very small numbers in scientific notation.
Convert scientific notation to standard decimal form.
Compare quantities using exponents and coefficients.
Interpret order of magnitude and significant digits.

lessons.title: Operations with Scientific Notation & Scale Applications
objectives: Multiply and divide numbers written in scientific notation.
Add and subtract scientific-notation values after aligning powers of ten.
Apply exponent properties to measurement and scale.
Report results with reasonable precision and units.

practice.title: Foundation Practice
practice.support: Hints and scaffolded powers, roots, and notation.

practice.title: Core Practice
practice.support: Complete practice across all Unit 6 domains.

practice.title: Extended Practice
practice.support: Proof, error analysis, precision, and unfamiliar scale models.
